story.value: Cadmium was discovered and first isolated by the German physician Friedrich Stromeyer in 1817.
The name comes from the Latin word cadmia and the Greek word kadmeia, the ancient name for calamine, which is zinc carbonate.
While studying calamine, Strohmeyer noticed that some samples glowed with a yellow color when heated, while other samples did not.

uses.value: Cadmium is used in rechargeable nickel-cadmium batteries.
Cadmium can be electroplated onto other materials to protect them from corrosion.
Cadmium sulfide, a cadmium compound, is a yellow powder that is used as a pigment.
Cadmium compounds are used in the phosphors of black and white televisions and in blue and green phosphors for color TV tubes.
